description: Tree 15–20 m high, 100–150 cm girth; bark grey or brownish, smooth, with spacing yellow lenticels, inner bark brownish-orange. Leaves opposite, digitately compound; leaflets (6–)7, unequal, the terminal one largest, oblanceolate, 12–35 by 5–12 cm, sub-coriaceous, glabrous; margin serrulate or double serrate; apex cuspidate; base cuneate; petiole terete, glabrous, 11–27 cm long; petiolules 0.25–2 cm long. Panicle including peduncle up to 70 cm long; composed of sub-helicoid 1.5–8 cm long cymes. Calyx 5-lobed, one is slightly larger than the other four, pubescent outside. Petals 4, white, yellow to orange towards the centre, obovate, 2–2.5 by ± 0.5 cm, glabrescent. Stamens 7, 3–4 cm long; anthers versatile. Fruits irregularly ovoid or ellipsoid, smooth, 2.5 cm across, brown with long stalk.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Aesculus assamica. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 395. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Tree, up to 45 m high and 0.75(–1.5) m diam. Leaves 6–17(–30)-jugate, 20–70 cm long; leaflets glabrous above, more or less pubescentbeneath, obliquely ovate-lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate, rarely ovate or oblong, falcate, acuminate (5–)9–15(–26) by 2.5–5.5 cm; nerves 8–20 pairs; at the end of the midrib beneath usually with a hairy gland, making the apex obtuse or even emarginate, apex rarely acute; on the undersurface often with acarodomatia in the nerve forks. Inflorescence paniculate, dense and many-flowered, more or less pubescent, ca 20–60 cm long; bracts small, ovate to triangular, caducous; pedicels up to ca 4 mm. Calyx pubescent, less than 1 mm high, lobes triangular, acute as long as the tube or a little longer. Petals glabrous or nearly so, ca 3–5 by 1–1.5 mm. Stamens: filaments tortuous-folded in bud, filiform or sometimes attenuate from the base to the top, usually with spreading hairs in the lower part, ca 3–6 mm long in male flowers, and ca 1–3 mm long in female flowers; anthers ca 1.2 by 1 mm in male flowers, smaller in female flowers flowers. Carpels (2–)3(–4), glabrous, ca 2–2.5 by 1–1.5 mm; styles free or coherent at the base, connate at the top, ca 1–1.5 mm: stigma (2–)3(–4)-lobed, peltate, ca 2 mm. diam. Fruit: samaras 1–3(–4), obtuse at the apex, main vascular bundle towards the seed intramarginal, scar of the style at the same level as the seed, ca 4.5–8 by 1.35–2.5 cm; pedicels 8–20 mm.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Ailanthus triphysa. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 440. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Shrub or small tree, 0.3–10 m, up to 10 cm diam. Leaves 20–50 cm long; leaflets 3–15, ovate-oblong to ovate-lanceolate, sparsely hairy above, more or less pubescent beneath, sometimes completely glabrous, 3.5–11 by 1.5–5 cm, the younger ones usually densely pubescent; margin bluntly serrate or crenate; nerves 6–15 pairs, parallel, ending in a marginal gland; petiole 5–10 cm, lateral petiolues 2–9 mm, terminal one 3–40 mm. Peduncle almost absent, rhachis 7–60 cm; bracts deltoid, small. Flowers greenish-white to greenish-red or purple. Male flowers: pedicels very slender, up to ca 3 mm long; sepals pubescent, sometimes toothed, ca 0.5–1 by 0.35–0.5 mm; petals sparsely pubescent to nearly glabrous, sometimes toothed, 1–2 by 0.5–1 mm; filaments subulate, ca 0.6 mm, anthers ca 0.4 mm long. Female flowers: pedicels up to 2.5 mm; sepals and petals as in male flowers. Stamens 0 or vestigial. Fruit: mature dried drupes 1–4 together, 4–5(–7) mm long; pedicels 2–6 mm; endosperm 0.2–0.5 mm thick.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Brucea javanica. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 442. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Shrub or small tree, 1–8 m, stem 3–10 cm diam. Leaves 20–60 cm long; leaflets 3–9(–13), ovate-oblong to ovate-lanceolate or lanceolate, entire, toothed, undulate, bluntly serrate, or crenate, glabrous or pubescent, 5–16 by 1–8 cm; nerves 4–9(–11) pairs, not parallel, usually anastomosing; petiole 2–13 cm, lateral petiolules 2–10 mm, terminal one 3–40 mm. Inflorescence and flowers as in B. javanica, but the pedicels of the female flowers up to 6 mm long. Flowers white, creamy, green, or red. Fruit: mature dried drupes 1–2(–3) together, 9–13 mm long; pedicels 4–10 mm; endosperm membranous.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Brucea mollis. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 442. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Robust, tall, erect herb, 1–5 m high; all parts viscid pubescent; stems slightly angular. Leaves opposite at base, spirally arranged upwards; stipules erect, filiform or narrowly subulate, ± 0.5 cm long, persistent; petioles 1.5–7 cm long, pubescent; lamina (3–)5–7(–11)-partite; upper ones often undivided, entire; segments narrowly lanceolate, serrate, 4–14 by 0.3–1.8 cm; upper surface scabrid with short, stiff hairs on systoliths, and pubescent with appressed hairs on the under surface; apex acuminate to caudate; base narrowly cuneate; nerves 8–20 pairs, reticulate veins inconspicuous. Male flowers in axillary or terminal panicles with few leaves. Tepals 5, free, finely pubescent, ± 5 mm long. Stamens 5, with slender filaments; anthers dehiscing by an apical pore. Female flowers solitary, axillary and terminal; each flower enveloped by a membranous spathe-like, dark green bract with glandular hairs. Perianth absent. Ovary 1-locular; style short divided into 2 long stigmatic arms; ovule 1. Fruit smooth, shining, yellowish or brownish, ovoid or ellipsoid, ± 4 mm long; seeds with fleshy endosperm.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Cannabis sativa. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 392. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Evergreen, dioecious tree, 10–15 m high, with conical-cylindric crown; lateral branches sweeping; switch-like twigs greyish-green, shallowly grooved, ± glabrous; internodes, 10–15 mm long. Leaves very small, tooth-like or scale-like, greenish-white, in whorls of 9–11 (rarely 12 or 13). Male inflorescence a cylindrical or slightly clavate spikes, 3–8 cm long; bracts hairy on the outer parts, bracteoles 1–2 with cuspidate apex. Female inflorescence an ellipsoid spike, 1–2 cm long. Infructescence cone-like, ellipsoid, truncate, 1.5–2 cm long; seeds many, winged, 4–5 mm long.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Casuarina junghuhniana. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 401. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Evergreen tree, up to 5 m high, twigs unarmed. Leaves (elliptic-)oblong, 8–18 by 4–7 cm, base rounded, apex acuminate or acute, chartaceous, glabrous on upper surface, sericeous, glabrescent on lower surface; brown when dry, secondary nerves 6–10 pairs, arched and anastomosing well away from the margin, depressed on upper surface, prominent on lower surface; scalariform veins inconspicuous on lower surface; petiole ± 3 mm long, tomentose. Male flowers cymose, 3-merous; pedicel 2–5 mm long. Calyx campanulate, 3–4 mm long, divided to the base, sericeous outside, glabrous inside. Corolla salver-shaped, 10–14 mm long, divided to one third, glabrous on both sides. Stamens 9–12, glabrous. Rudimentary ovary glabrous. Female flowers cymose, 3-merous; pedicel 3–15 mm long, tomentose. Calyx campanulate, divided to one half or three fifths, tomentose outside, glabrous inside. Corolla urceolate, divided to one third, ± glabrous on both sides. Ovary ovoid, glabrous, 6-locular; style single, glabrous. Staminodes absent. Fruit ovoid or ellipsoid, 1.5–2.5 by 1.5–2 cm, woody, ± glabrous, base acute, rounded or truncate, apex obtuse or rounded; fruiting calyx divided ± to the base, pubescent outside, glabrous inside, lobes triangular, ± 2.5 by 2 mm, not reflexed, not plicate nor undulate, without nerves; fruit-stalk ± 5 mm long, tomentose; endosperm ruminate or smooth.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Diospyros andamanica. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 301. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Evergreen tree, up to 5 m high, twigs unarmed. Leaves ovate-oblong orovate-lanceolate, 10–15 by 3.5–4.5 cm, base rounded or cordate, apex apiculate or cuspidate, subcoriaceous to coriaceous, tomentose on upper surface and hispid on lower surface later glabrescent except along midrib and nerves on both surfaces; lateral veins 6–8 pairs, arched and ± anastomosing well away from the margin, ± impressed on upper surface, prominent on lower surface; reticulation ± impressed on upper surface, inconspicuous on lower surface; petiole 4–5 mm long, hispid, glabrescent. Male flowers cymose, 4(–5)-merous, sessile or subsessile. Calyx campanulate, divided to or nearly to the base, ± 5 mm long, hispid on both sides. Corolla salver-shaped, divided to one third, 8–10 mm long, glabrous on both sides. Stamens 6–12, 4–6 mm long glabrous. Rudimentary ovary long hairy. Female flowers solitary 4(–5)-merous, subsessile. Calyx and Corolla as in male flowers but larger. Ovary ovoid, sericeous, 4-locular; styles 2, sericeous. Staminodes absent. Fruit sessile, conical or ovoid, 1.5–2 by 1–1.5 cm, sericeous, glabrescent at maturity except around apex, base rounded, apex acute; fruiting calyx divided to or nearly to the base, pubescent on both sides; lobes ovate-oblong, 5–10 by 3–5 mm, not reflexed, not plicate nor undulate, without nerves; endosperm smooth.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Diospyros apiculata. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 376. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Evergreen tree, up to 15 m high; young twigs ± glabrous, unarmed. Leaves oblong, 7–20 by 4–7 cm, base rounded, apex acute, rarely obtuse, coriaceous, glabrous on both surfaces or only pilose along midrib on lower surface; secondary nerves 6–12 pairs, not anastomosing, inconspicuous on both surfaces; reticulation usually conspicuous only on upper surface indistinct on lower surface; petiole 1–1.5 cm long, pilose. Male flowers cymose; not cauliflorous; 4(–5)-merous; pedicel ± 2 mm long, tomentose. Calyx broadly campanulate, ± 3 mm long, divided to a quarter, glabrous on both sides. Corolla urceolate or ovoid, divided to a quarter, ± 7 mm long, tube glabrous on both sides, lobes pubescent outside, entirely glabrous inside. Stamens 20–21; filaments glabrous, 2.5–3.5 mm long; anthers sparsely hairy along the mid-line. Rudimentary ovary covered with long hairs. Female flowers solitary or cymose, 4-merous; pedicels 5–10 mm long, densely hairy. Calyx campanulate, ± 3 mm long, divided to a fifth, woolly on both sides. Corolla as in male flowers but larger. Ovary ovoid, hispid, 8-locular; styles 2, glabrous; stigmas 4. Staminodes ± 20, glabrous. Fruit ovoid or globose, 3–5 by 2.5–3.5 cm, more or less succulent and not fragrant when ripe, pericarp ± 1 mm thick, sparsely covered with dark red caducous scales, base rounded or slightly cuneate, apex rounded; fruiting calyx divided to or nearly to the base, glabrous or puberulous on both sides; lobes usually reflexed, rarely ascending, plicate, ± undulate, with inconspicuous nerves; fruit-stalk ± 1 cm long; endosperm smooth.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Diospyros areolata. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 334. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Evergreen tree, up to 20 m high; sapwood white. Leaves oblong orelliptic-oblong, 3.5–8 by 1.5–2.5 cm, base obtuse, rarely acute, apex obtuse, rarely acute, chartaceous; upper surface glabrous, except pubescent midrib; lower surface sparsely sericeous, glabrescent; secondary nerves 6–12 pairs, 40°–50° degrees to midrib, arched and anastomosing well away from the margin, conspicuous on both surfaces; reticulation conspicuous only on upper surface; petiole ±2 mm long, pubescent. Male flowers cymose, 3-merous, sessile. Calyx campanulate, 1–2 mm long, divided to middle, glabrous on both sides. Corolla broadly campanulate or ovoid, 2–3 mm long, divided to middle; tube glabrous on both sides, lobes pubescent then glabrescent outside, glabrous inside. Stamens 16–20, glabrous. Rudimentary ovary glabrous. Female flowers sessile, not sufficiently known.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Diospyros bambuseti. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 290. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Evergreen tree, up to 10 m high, twigs unarmed. Leaves ovate or oblong, 3–15 by 1.5–5 cm, olive-green or blackish when dry, base rounded, apex acute or acuminate with blunt tip, coriaceous, glabrous on both surfaces; secondary nerves 8–15 pairs, arched and anastomosing well away from the margin, inconspicuous on both surfaces; reticulation prominent on both surfaces; petiole 3–10 mm long, glabrous. Male flowers cymose, 4-merous, sessile or subsessile. Calyx campanulate, 4–6 mm long, divided to a quarter or up to half way, tomentose outside, glabrous inside. Corolla salver-shaped, 1–1.5 cm long, divided to a quarter, sericeous outside, glabrous inside. Stamens 14–20, glabrous. Rudimentary ovary hirsute. Female flowers solitary, 4-merous, subsessile. Calyx campanulate, divided to middle, sericeous on both sides. Corolla as in male flowers but larger. Ovary globose, sericeous, 8-locular; style simple, sericeous. Staminodes 4. Fruit globose, 2–2.5 by 3–3.5 cm, dry at maturity, epicarp ± 1 mm thick, brittle when dry, glabrous, strongly depressed at both ends; fruiting calyx divided to half way, tomentose, glabrescent on both sides; lobes not reflexed; but limb recurved undulate and plicate, without nerves; fruit-stalk 2–3 mm long or invisible; endosperm ruminate.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Diospyros bejaudii. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 378. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Evergreen tree, up to 25 m high, twigs unarmed. Leaves elliptic, ovate or oblong, 12–20 by 4–9 cm; base obtuse or rounded, sometimes truncate, apex acuminate or obtuse, chartaceous to subcoriaceous, greenish when dry, glabrous on upper surface, pubescent on lower surface; secondary nerves 5–12 pairs, arched and anastomosing well away from the margin, impressed on upper surface, prominent on lower surface; scalariform veins ± impressed on upper surface, inconspicuous on lower surface; petiole ± 1 cm long, pubescent. Male flowers cymose, 5-merous; pedicel 3–10 mm long, pubescent. Calyx cylindrical or funnel-shaped, 5–7 mm long, entire, pubescent on both sides. Corolla tubular, 1.5–1.7 cm long, divided to middle, pubescent outside, glabrous inside. Stamens 15–25, glabrous. Rudimentary ovary hispid. Female flowers solitary, 5-merous; pedicel 5–10 mm long, pubescent. Calyx and Corolla as in male flowers but larger, and calyx divided to or nearly to base. Ovary ovoid, hispid, 12–14–16-locular; styles 2, hispid. Staminodes 10, glabrous. Fruit globose, 4–5 by 4–5 cm, pericarp woody, 2–5 mm thick, tomentose, later glabrescent, base rounded, apex rounded, shortly apiculate; fruiting calyx divided to the base or nearly so, glabrous outside, pubescent or tomentose inside, limbs slightly reflexed, but apex erect, not undulate nor plicate, without nerves; fruit-stalk ± 1 cm long; endosperm smooth.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Diospyros borneensis. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 359. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Evergreen tree, up to 15 m high. Leaves (lanceolate-) oblong or lanceolate, 14–20 by 3.5–6 cm, base acute or obtuse, apex cuspidate with blunt tip or acuminate, chartaceous, glabrous on both surfaces, except along midrib and secondary nerves on lower surface; lateral veins 13–18 pairs, arched but not anastomosing, impressed on upper surface, prominent on lower surface; scalariform veins finely prominent on lower surface; petiole ± 5 mm long, pubescent. Male flowers cymose (usually on trunk), 5-merous; pedicel 2–5 mm long, pubescent. Calyx broadly campanulas, 2–3 mm long, divided to or nearly to the base, lobes not plicate nor undulate, sparsely blackish- tomentose outside, glabrous inside. Corolla salver-shaped, 2–2.2 cm long, lobes as long as the tube and glabrous on both sides; tube sparsely blackish-tomentose outside and glabrous inside. Stamens 14–16, anthers glabrous, filaments sericeous. Rudimentary ovary hirsute. Female flowers solitary or cymose (usually on trunk), 5-merous, sessile or subsessile. Calyx campanulate, erect, lobes as long as the tube, not plicate nor undulate, pubescent outside, glabrous inside. Corolla salver-shaped, divided to two fifths; tomentose outside, glabrous inside. Ovary ovoid, tomentose, 10-locular; style single, tomentose. Staminodes 4–5, anthers glabrous, filaments sericeous. Fruit (very young) ovoid, pubescent, base obtuse, apex obtuse, shortly apiculate.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Diospyros brandisiana. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 373. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Evergreen tree, up to 25 m high, twigs unarmed. Leaves elliptic, subrhomboid or ovate, subsessile, 1.2–4 by 0.5–2 cm, base acute, obtuse or rounded, apex acute, obtuse or mucronate, chartaceous, brown when dry, glabrous except pubescent along midrib on upper surface, sericeous later glabrescent, except along midrib on lower surface; secondary nerves inconspicuous. Male flowers cymose or solitary, 4-merous, sessile. Calyx campanulate, 2–3 mm long, divided to half or three fifths, pubescent outside, glabrous inside. Corolla campanulate, 2–4 mm long, divided to two thirds, glabrous on both sides, pubescent along mid-line of lobes outside. Stamens 8–20; anthers glabrous; filaments pilose. Rudimentary ovary pilose. Female flowers solitary, 4-merous; pedicel 1–2 mm long, pubescent. Calyx and Corolla as in male flowers, but larger. Ovary conical, glabrous, 4-locular; styles 2, pubescent in the lower half. Staminodes absent. Fruit ellipsoid or conical, 1–1.5 by 0.4–1 cm, dry, ± glabrous, obtuse at both ends; fruiting calyx campanulate, divided to middle; pubescent outside, glabrous inside; lobes not reflexed, neither plicate nor undulate and with inconspicuous nerves; fruit-stalk ± 5 mm long; endosperm smooth.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Diospyros buxifolia. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 305. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Deciduous tree, up to 15 m high. Leaves ovate, oval or elliptic, 6–13 by 2.5–8 cm, base rounded, truncate or sub-cordate, apex obtuse acute or emarginate, subcoriaceous to coriaceous, glabrous on both surfaces; secondary nerves 6–10 pairs, rather ascending and not anastomosing, faint, ± impressed on upper surface and prominent on lower surface; tertiary veins ± indistinct; petiole 4–10 mm long, glabrous. Male flowers cymose, 3-merous, sessile. Calyx oblong, 3–5 mm long, divided to one tenth, sericeous outside, ± glabrous inside. Corolla oblong, 10–12 mm long, lobes as long as tube and pubescent on both sides, tube glabrous on both sides. Stamens 12–14, glabrous. Rudimentary ovary glabrous. Female flowers solitary or cymose, 3-merous; pedicel 2–3 mm long, glabrous. Calyx and Corolla as in male flowers but larger. Ovary ovoid, pubescent, 6-locular; style single, pubescent. Staminodes absent. Fruit ellipsoid to globose, 2–3 by 1.5–3 cm, woody, epicarp 2 mm thick or more, glabrous or pubescent near base; base rounded or slightly cuneate, apex rounded with short cusp; fruiting calyx divided to one third, pubescent outside, glabrous inside; lobes with the limb minutely undulate and reflexed, not plicate, and without nerves; fruit-stalk ± 5 mm long; endosperm ruminate.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Diospyros castanea. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 299. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Evergreen tree, up to 8 m high, twigs unarmed. Leaves oblong or lanceolate, 11–15 by 3–8 cm, base acute or slightly cuneate, apex cuspidate or caudate, chartaceous to subcoriaceous, glabrous on both surfaces; secondary nerves 8–12 pairs, arched and anastomosing well away from the margin, impressed on upper surface, prominent on lower surface; scalariform veins inconspicuous on lower surface; reticulate veins indistinct; petiole 5–10 mm long, pubescent later glabrescent. Male flowers cymose (usually tufted on trunk), 4(–5)-merous; pedicel 2–5 mm long, densely black-hairy. Calyx campanulate, ± 2 mm long, divided to two thirds, black-hairy outside, glabrous inside. Corolla ovoid or urceolate, 2–3 mm long, divided to a quarter; tomentose or woolly outside, glabrous inside. Stamens 16–20, pubescent. Rudimentary ovary hirsute. Female flowers cymose or solitary (usually on trunk), 4(–5)-merous; pedicel 2–3 mm long, pubescent. Calyx broadly campanulate, divided to half or to three fifths, pubescent outside, glabrous inside. Corolla ovoid or urceolate, divided to a thrid, woolly outside, glabrous inside. Ovary ovoid, tomentose, 6-locular; style solitary, tomentose. Staminodes 8–10, glabrous. Fruit on trunk and branches, ovoid or ellipsoid, 1.5–3 by 1.5–2.5 cm, leathery woody, glabrous, rounded or obtuse at both ends, minutely apiculate at apex; fruiting calyx divided to the base, pubescent on both sides; lobes reflexed and undulate but not plicate and with inconspicuous nerves; fruit-stalk 3–5 mm long; endosperm smooth.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Diospyros cauliflora. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 332. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Evergreen tree, up to 6 m high; terminal bud with black hairs. Leaves oblong, oblanceolate, 15–23 by 4–6 cm, base obtuse or slightly acute, apex acute to acuminate, rarely rounded, coriaceous, glabrous except for sparsely blackish hairs along midrib and nerves on lower surface; lateral veins 9–12 pairs, arched and anastomosing well away from the margin, conspicuous on both sides; reticulation fine, prominent on upper surface, conspicuous on lower surface; petiole 1–1.4 cm long, sparsely pilose later glabrescent. Male flowers cymose, 4-merous; pedicel ± 4 mm long, tomentose. Calyx ovoid, 4–6 mm long, divided to one sixth, tomentose outside, glabrous inside. Corolla urceolate or ovoid, 6–8 mm long, divided to a quarter, pubescent outside, glabrous inside. Stamens 14–20, glabrous. Rudimentary ovary sericeous. Female flowers and fruit unknown.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Diospyros collinsiae. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 385. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Evergreen tree, up to 20 m high, twigs unarmed. Leaves oblong orelliptic, 4–11 by 1.5–4 cm, base obtuse or acute and always oblique, apex cuspidate or acuminate with blunted point, subcoriaceous or coriaceous, glabrous on both surfaces; secondary nerves 8–10 pairs, 70°–80° degrees to midrib, faintly anastomosing well away from the margin, conspicuous on both surfaces; reticulation inconspicuous; petiole 3–4 mm long, pubescent then glabrescent. Male flowers cymose, 3-merous, sessile or subsessile. Calyx campanulate, 2–3 mm long, divided to or nearly to the base, pubescent outside, glabrous inside. Corolla urceolate, 4–7 mm long; lobes as long as corolla-tube, woolly outside, glabrous inside. Stamens 9–12, glabrous. Rudimentary ovary glabrous. Female flowers solitary or cymose, 3-merous; pedicel 1–2 mm long, pubescent. Calyx campanulate, divided to two fifth up to half way, pubescent outside, glabrous inside. Corolla as in male flowers but larger. Ovary ovoid, glabrous, 6-locular; style single, glabrous. Staminodes 3–6, ± glabrous. Fruit awn-shaped, 2–2.5 by 1–1.5 cm, woody, glabrous, base obtuse or acute, apex mucronate or acuminate; fruiting calyx divided to the base, pubescent then glabrescent outside, glabrous inside; lobes reflexed, not undulate nor plicate, without nerves; fruit-stalk ± 3 mm long; endosperm smooth.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Diospyros confertiflora. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 292. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Evergreen tree, up to 10 m high, twigs unarmed. Leaves (oblong-) obovate, 7–15 by 2.5–4.5 cm, base acute or slightly cuneate, apex acuminate, cuspidate with blunt point, coriaceous, glabrous on both surfaces; midrib always orange when dry, secondary nerves 8–12 pairs, faintly anastomosing well away from the margin, inconspicuous on both surfaces; reticulation prominent on upper surface, inconspicuous on lower surface; petiole ± 3 mm long, glabrous. Male flowers cymose, 4(–5)-merous; pedicel 2–3 mm long, pubescent. Calyx campanulate, 2–4 mm long, divided to middle; pubescent outside, ± glabrous inside. Corolla urceolate or ovoid, 4–7 mm long, divided to middle, pubescent outside, glabrous inside. Stamens 16–18, glabrous. Rudimentary ovary hirsute. Female flowers solitary or cymose, 4(–5)-merous; pedicel ± 2 mm long, pubescent. Calyx campanulate, divided to the base, glabrous on both sides. Corolla ovoid, divided to the base, pubescent outside, glabrous inside. Ovary ovoid, tomen tose, 4-locular; style single, tomentose. Staminodes 8–10, glabrous. Fruit globose, ca 2 cm diam. pericarp crustaceous, glabrous, base rounded or ± depressed, apex rounded with short cusp; fruiting calyx divided ± to the base, ± glabrous on both sides, lobes (apex) ascending, but margin reflexed, undulate and ± plicate, with inconspicuous nerves; fruit-stalk 5–10 mm long; endosperm smooth.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Diospyros curranii. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 310. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Evergreen tree, up to 20 m high, twigs unarmed. Leaves (ovate-)lanceolate, 10–12 by 2–2.5 cm, base acute, or obtuse, apex cuspidate, chartaceous, glabrous on both surfaces; lateral veins 8–12 pairs, curved and anastomosing well away from the margin, prominent on both surfaces; reticulation prominent on upper surface, inconspicuous on lower surface; petiole 5–10 mm long, glabrous. description: Evergreen tree, up to 20 m high; twigs pubescent; stipulescaducous. Leaves elliptic or oblong, 7–11 by 2.5–4.5 cm, serrate or nearly entire; base acute or obtuse; apex acuminate or cuspidate; glabrous on upper surface, pubescent-glabrescent on lower surface; secondary nerves 4–6 pairs, arched but not anastomosing, slightly prominent on lower surface; petiole 1.2–3 cm long, pubescent-glabrescent, usually geniculate. Inflorescences in axils of present leaves, 3–10 cm long; pedicels 3–7 mm long, pubescent. Sepals lanceolate or narrowly triangular, ± 3 by 1 mm, pubescent on both surfaces. Petals wedge-shaped, ± 3 by 2 mm, without basal ridge inside, glabrous; laciniae about ½ the length of the petal, with glandular apex. Stamens 10–16, ± 1 mm long, glabrous; anthers not aristate. Ovary ovoid, pubescent, 5-locular; style pubescent at the lower half only; disc distinctly 5-lobed. Drupes woody, globose, ± 2.5 by 2.5 cm, glabrous, round at both ends; fruit stalks ± 1 cm long glabrous; seed 1–3, embryo straight.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Elaeocarpus nitidus. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 438. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Evergreen tree, up to 30 m high; twigs glabrous. Leaves elliptic or oblong, 9–23 by 4–10 cm, not strongly serrate, glabrous; base obtuse or acute; apex acute, acuminate or cuspidate; secondary nerves 5–8 pairs, arched but not anastomosing, distinct and often with domatia in axils on lower surface; petiole 3.5–10 cm long, glabrous, usually geniculate. Inflorescences in axils of present leaves, 5–10 cm long; pedicels 0.8–1 cm long, pubescent-glabrescent. Sepals lanceolate, ± 6 by 2 mm, pubescent-glabrescent outside, glabrous inside. Petals oblong, ± 6 by 2 mm, hairy on both sides, with one hairy basal ridge inside, about ⅖ the length; laciniae about ⅖ the length of the petal and usually not spreading. Stamens 25–31, 4 mm long, pilose; anthers aristate at apex. Ovary conical or ovoid, glabrous, 2-locular; style glabrous; disc distinctly 10-lobed. Drupes ellipsoid, obtuse at both ends, 1.2–2 by 0.8–1 cm, with thin epicarp, glabrous; fruit stalks ± 1.5 cm long, glabrous; seed 1, embryo straight.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Elaeocarpus petiolatus. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 424. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Evergreen tree, up to 25 m high; apical part of young twigs notresionous; twigs pubescent, glabrescent. Leaves ovate, ellipitic or oblong, 8–25 by 4–13 cm, crenate, rarely shallowly serrate; base rounded or obtuse; apex cuspidate, acute or rounded; hairy along midrib on both surfaces; secondary nerves 8–12 pairs, ascending, prominent on lower surface, often with hairy domatia in axils on lower surface; petiole 1.5–6 cm long, pubescent, glabrescent, usually geniculate and swollen at both ends. Inflorescences below the leaves in axils of fallen leaves, 6–21 cm long; pedicels 0.4–1 cm long, pubescent. Sepals ovate-lanceolate, ± 5 by 2 mm, pubescent outside, hairy along limb and median line inside. Petals obovate, ± 7 by 4 mm, ciliate in lower half; without basal ridge inside; laciniae about ½ the length of petals. Stamens 30–40, ± 3 mm long, glabrous; anthers not aristate, glabrous at apex. Ovary ovoid, stiffly hairy, 3-locular; style stiffly hairy in lower half disc distinctly 5-lobed. Drupes woody, ellipsoid, 3–3.5 by 2–2.3 cm, obtuse or acute at both ends, grey pubescent; fruit-stalks 1–1.5 cm long, grey pubescent; seeds 1–3, embryo straight.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Elaeocarpus robustus. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 419. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Evergreen tree, up to 20 m high; twigs long hairy, glabrescent. Stipules caducous. Leaves obovate or oblanceolate, 10–45 by 4–18 cm, serrate, always spiny at the tips; base slightly cuneate, insertion truncate; apex obtuse or apiculate; glabrous on upper surface, long-hairy, glabrescent on lower surface; secondary nerves 15–25 pairs, ascending, prominent on both surfaces; petiole 1.5–3 cm long, covered with long hairs. Inflorescences usually below the leaves in axils of fallen leaves, 7–12 cm long; pedicels 2–3 cm long, long-hairy. Sepals lanceolate, 1.5–2 by 0.3–0.4 cm, long-hairy outside, only hairy along median line inside. Petals obovate, 1.5–2 by 0.8–1 cm, long-hairy on both sides; with 2 basal hairy ridges inside, each about ½ the length; laciniae about ⅛ the length of the petal. Stamens numerous, ± 1.3 cm long, hairy, anthers aristate at apex. Ovary ovoid, long-hairy: 2-locular, style long-hairy, disc entire or slightly lobed. Drupes ellipsoid, 3–4 by 1.5–2 cm, woody, pubescent, glabrescent; fruit-stalk 2–3 cm long, pubescent, glabrescent; seeds 1, embryo straight.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Elaeocarpus rugosus. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 410. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Evergreen tree, up to 25 m high; twigs pubescent. Leaves (lanceolate-) oblong, sometimes suboblanceolate, 10–17 by 3–5 cm, serrulate; base acute or obtuse; apex acute or acuminate; glabrous on upper surface, pubescent, glabrescent on lower surface; secondary nerves 8–13 pairs, arched but not anastomosing, depressed on upper surface, prominent on lower surface, often with domatia in axils on lower surface; petiole ± 1 cm long, pubescent. Inflorescences below the leaves, in axils of fallen leaves, 6–10 cm long; pedicels ± 1 cm long, pubescent. Sepals lanceolate, ± 8 by 2 mm, pubescent outside, only ciliate along limb inside. Petals (obovate-) oblong, 10–20 by 3–5 mm, pubescent outside, long ciliate, inside smooth and glabrous; laciniae about one half the length of the petal. Stamens numerous, ± 8 mm long, sparsely hairy, anthers aristate at apex. Ovary ovoid, covered with long hairs, 5-locular; style covered with long hairs in lower half only; disc distinctly 5-lobed. Drupes woody, globose, ± 2.5 by 2.5 cm, pubescent later glabrescent, rounded or truncate at both ends; fruit-stalk ± 1 cm long, glabrous; seeds 2–5, embryo straight.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Elaeocarpus sphaericus. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 412. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Evergreen tree, up to 30 m high; twigs shortly hairy. Stipules often persistent.Leaves oblong, elliptic, or ovate, 7–25 by 3–9 cm, serrate, serrulate or crenate to entire; base obtuse, acute or rounded; apex cuspidate rarely obtuse or rounded; only hairy along midrib on the upper surface, with dense stiff hairs on lower surface; secondary nerves 8–14 pairs, ± ascending, ± depressed on upper surface, prominent on lower surface; often with domatia in nerve axils on lower surface; petiole 1–6 cm, pubescent. Inflorescences in leaf axils or in axils of fallen leaves below the leaves, 8–10 cm long; pedicels 0.5–1 cm long, pubescent. Sepals ovate-oblong, 5–6 by 2 mm with short, stiff hairs outside, pubescent, glabrescent inside. Petals spathulate, 5–6 by 4–5 mm, ciliate in lower half, with one basally hairy ridge inside, ridge about ⅓ the length; laciniae about ⅓ the length of the petal. Stamens numerous, ± 3 mm long, glabrous; anthers with a tuft of hairs at apex, apex not aristate. Ovary ovoid, covered with long hairs, 3–(5)-locular; style long-hairy in lower half only; disc distinctly 5-lobed. Drupes woody, globose or ellipsoid, 1.5–3.5 by 1.5–3 cm, shortly hairy, later glabrescent, rounded at both ends; fruit-stalks ± 1 cm long, with short stiff hairs; seeds 1–3, embryo straight.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Elaeocarpus stipularis. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 415. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Evergreen tree, up to 8 m high; apical part of young twigs resinous; twigs pubescent-glabrescent. Leaves (obovate-) oblong, 11–23 by 4–9 cm, serrate; base acute or obtuse; apex cuspidate; glabrous on both sides, hairy along midrib on lower surface; secondary nerves 8–12 pairs, ascending, depressed on upper surface, prominent on lower surface; scalariform veins fine, prominent on lower surface; petiole 2.5–7 cm long, glabrous. Inflorescences in axils of present leaves, 8–12 cm long; pedicels 0.8–1.2 cm long, pubescent. Sepals narrowly lanceolate, ± 12 by 2 mm, pubescent on both sides. Petals oblong ± 12 by 3 mm, covered with long hairs on both sides, with 3 basal hairy ridges inside, hairs directed towards the base, each ridge about the length of the petal, laciniae about ¼ the length. Stamens numerous, 6–8 mm long, pubescent; anthers aristate at apex. Ovary ovoid, covered with long hairs, 3-locular; style long hairy in lower half only; disc distinctly 10-lobed. Drupes ovoid or ellipsoid, ± 1.2 by 0.5 cm, dry with thin epicarp, glabrous, rounded at both ends; fruit stalks ± 1.5 cm long, pubescent-glabrescent; seed 1, embryo straight.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Elaeocarpus varunua. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 432. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Dwarf shrub. Leaves to ca 18 cm long; leaflets 3–7 cm by 3–5 mm. Panicles pubescent, not glandular hairy, to 15 cm long. Calyx lobes 1–1.5 mm. Petals 3–3.5 by 1–1.5 mm, pubescent at both faces. Stamens 5; filaments pubescent, ca 2 mm long; anthers ca 0.75 mm. Ovary reduced, pubescent (only male flowers seen).
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Eurycoma harmandiana. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 444. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Leaves up to ca 1 m long; leaflets lanceolate to obovate-lanceolate, rarely ovate-oblong, sometimes slightly acuminate with a bluntish or acute apex, ca 5–20 by 1.5–6 cm. Branches of inflorescence, pedicels, sepals, and calyx puberulous and with capitate-glandular hairs. Flowers reddish; bracts triangular, very small, up toe. 1 mm, caducous; pedicels rather thick, up to ca 7 mm. Calyx small, lobes ca 1 mm long. Petals puberulous on both surfaces, lanceolate to ovate- or obovate-oblong, ca 4–5–5.5 by 2–3 mm. Stamens usually longer than the calyx, ca 1.5–2.5 mm long, anthers ca 0.25 mm long; staminodes from 0.5 mm in female flowers to ca 2 mm in male flowers. Styles rather long, with a peltate 5(–6)-lobed stigma, elevated ca 1 mm above the ovaries. Fruits 10–17(–20) by 5–12 mm.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Eurycoma longifolia. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 444. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Leaves 1–15-jugate, up to ca 20 cm; rhachis narrowly winged, usually with a ribabove, more or less pubescent, especially above; leaflets 10–20 by 5–15 mm; petiole 0.5–3 cm. Branches of cymes and thyrses for some length adnate to the peduncle; pedicels up to 2 mm. Calyx ca 1.5 mm high, lobes ca 0.75 mm. Petals lanceolate, rarely oblong, 6–9 by 2–4 mm. Stamens: anthers ca 1.5–4.5 mm; filaments 7–10 mm; ligule densely woolly at the margin, ca 2 mm. Disk cup-shaped, 1–2 mm high. Ovary 0.5–1 mm high, slightly lobed; style pubescent, 5–8 mm. Fruit 4–9 by 11–15 mm; exocarp coriaceous, at least 1 mm thick; endocarp hard, without a suture.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Harrisonia perforata. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 445. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Tree, up to 40 m high; bark dark grey, smooth or shallowly fissured, lenticellate, producing poisonous sap; wood white or yellowish; twigs tomentose, glabrescent with stiff hairs. Leaves oblong, elliptic or obovate, 5–20 by 3–9 cm; base slightly cuneate or acute; apex acuminate, obtuse or rounded, subcoriaceous; glabrous except along midrib on upper surface, sparsely hairy to densely hairy on lower surface, later glabrescent; secondary nerves 8–15 pairs, 40°–50° to midrib; petioles 1–3.5 cm long, flattened, with stiff hairs, glabrescent. Flowers in ± globose, axillary heads. Calyx campanulate, densely hairy outside, lobes triangular. Petals yellowish or greenish, obovate, glabrous, recurved. Male heads 20–40-flowered; pedicels short; peduncle slender, 0.5–3 cm long, pubescent. Stamens 8–10. Female heads with 3–8 (rarely up to 18) sessile flowers; peduncle similar to male ones; staminodes 8–10. Drupes ellipsoid, 1.5–2.5 cm long, more or less laterally flattened; exocarp with sparse yellowish dots; seeds flattened, obovate, acute, on one side with 5 lengthwise grooves, other side with few tubercles on upper half.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Nyssa javanica. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 402. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Tree, up to 20 m, bole up to 15 m and 35 cm diam; bark grey to brown, smooth, fissured. Leaves 2–3(–4)-jugate; petiole 2–6 cm, as the rhachis terete, sparsely puberulous to glabrous; petiolules 0–7 mm; leaflets entire, sometimes with a waved or wrinkled margin, usually rather abruptly blunt-acuminate, cuneate at the base, 4–20 by 1–10 cm; nerves 3–8 pairs; on upper surface midrib crested, nerves narrowly sulcate, venation indistinct; underneath nerves and reticulate venation prominent; stipules foliaceous, flabellately veined, nearly orbicular with rounded apex and acute base, 7–25 by 5–20 mm, usually early caducous, leaving a rather large scar. Inflorescences up to 20 cm long, planoconvex; bracts obovate, rounded, very early caducous. Flowers 4-merous, white to yellow or green; pedicels ca 10 mm in female and up to 7 mm in male flowers. Sepals glabrous to puberulous, triangular to ovate, acutish, ca 1 mm. Petals ovate-oblong or oblong, often acute-acuminate to mucronate, glabrous to sparsely hairy, with a conspicuous midrib, in male flowers 2–5 by 1–2 mm; in female flowers 3–7 by 3–5 mm, accrescent to 10–15(–20) by ca 7(–10) mm. Disk hairy, 4-lobed, 0.5–1 mm high. Stamens usually longer than petals in male flowers, shorter than petals in female flowers; filaments gradually thinner towards the top, hairy at the base, 0.5–2 mm in female, 1–5 mm in male flowers; anthers 1–2 by 0.75–1.5 mm in male and up to 1 by 0.5 mm and barren in female flowers. Carpels up to 4, glabrous or puberulous; styles 1–1.5 mm; stigmas ca 2 mm. Drupes 1–4, green to red or blue, ovoid to depressed-globose, ca 9–10 by 7–12 mm.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Picrasma javanica. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 447. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Evergreen tree, up to 30 m high; twigs glabrous. Leaves ovate, obovate, elliptic or oblong, 7–22 by 3.5–8.5 cm; rounded, truncate or slightly cuneate at base; apex cuspidate; chartaceous, ± glabrous, margin entire; nerves 5–8 pairs, arched and anastomosing, ± depressed on upper surface, prominent on lower surface; reticulate and scalariform veins prominent on lower surface; petiole 1–5 cm long, glabrous, swollen at both ends. Flowers 4-merous; pedicel 1–5 cm long, glabrous. Sepals ovate, pubescent on both sides. Petals ovate or obovate, yellowish, ± sparsely hairy on both sides. Stamens 5–7 mm long. Ovary ovoid, sparsely hairy; style glabrous. Capsule globose, 5–6 cm across (including the ± 10 mm long prickles); fruit-stalk 1–7 cm long.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Sloanea sigun. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 406. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Deciduous tree up to 30 m high; twigs tomentose later glabrescent. Leaveselliptic or ovate, usually not symmetric, 11–20 by 5.5–12.5 cm; base rounded or obtuse; apex rounded or shortly cuspidate, coriaceous, tomentose; margin entire; nerves 7–9 pairs, ± arched and anastomosing, depressed on upper surface, prominent on lower surface; reticulate and scalariform veins prominent on lower surface; petiole 2.5–3.5 cm long, densely covered with short hairs, later glabrescent. Flowers 5-merous; pedicel 1–3 cm long, densely covered with short hairs. Sepals ovate, pubescent on both sides. Petals oval or obovate, yellowish, ± pubescent on both sides. Stamens ± 6 mm long. Ovary ovoid, sparsely hairy; style glabrous near the top. Capsule globose, ± 4.5 cm across (including the ± 1–2 mm long prickles); fruit-stalk 2–3 cm long.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Sloanea tomentosa. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 406. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Shrub or tree to 20 m, 50 cm diam; young twigs puberulous or rarelytomentellous, glabrescent; terminal buds hairy. Leaves chartaceous to coriaceous, often dark brown when dry, pulverulent beneath or on both faces, soon glabrescent, elliptic, acuminate, with cuneate base and recurved to revolute margin with many pellucid glands, 4.5–16 by 1.2–4.7 cm, acumen 7–35 mm; nerves 4–12 pairs, meeting in a looped intramarginal vein; reticulation often fine; petiole 6–12 mm. Flowers in a spike, raceme or panicle to 6 cm; indumentum of axis as of twigs; bracts and bracteoles with same indumentum, persistent in fruit, 0.5–1 mm; pedicels mostly under older flowers, to 3 mm. Calyx nearly entirely divided into 0.5–1 mm long lobes. Corolla 2–5 mm. Stamens (20–)25–50. Disk glabrous or rarely hairy. Ovary with same indumentum as that of twigs, 1–2 mm high; style glabrous or with some hairs towards the base, 2–4 mm. Fruit ellipsoid to cylindrical, sometimes with ca 6 ridges when dry, soon glabrescent, crowned by the incurved calyx lobes, with only one developed cell, 8–10(–11) by 3–5(–6) mm; mesocarp thin, coriaceous. Seed 1, with straight embryo.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Symplocos adenophylla. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 452. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Shrub or tree to 21 m; young twigs tomentellous to tomentose orappressed pubescent, glabrescent; terminal buds hairy. Leaves glabrous, brownish or olive to yellowish green, glossy above, elliptic, acuminate with cuneate-attenuate base and more or less revolute finely glandular dentate to nearly entire margin, 2.5–12 by 1.2–3 cm; acumen 2–20 mm; midrib above prominent or flat, rarely flat and sunken; nerves 5–11 pairs, meeting in a looped intramarginal vein; petiole 2–7 mm. Raceme to 2 cm long, axis tomentose to appressed-pubescent; bracts 1–2 mm; bracteoles 0.25–1.5 mm, both persistent, with same indumentum as on axis; pedicels 2–5 mm. Calyx lobes rounded, ciliolate, 0.5–2 mm. Corolla 4–6 mm. Stamens 50 to more than 100. Disk tomentose or shortly soft-hairy. Ovary tomentose to (finely) appressed-pubescent, ca 0.5–1.5 mm high; style glabrous or hairy towards the base, 4–7 mm. Fruit 3-celled, ellipsoid, ca 10 by 6 mm; mesocarp fleshy, thin, stone faintly ribbed. Seed 1 in each cell, straight, with straight embryo.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Symplocos anomala. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 453. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Shrub or small tree, rarely up to 30 m high and 40 cm diam; twigs glabrous; terminal buds glabrous or pubescents. Leaves glabrous, or rarely sparsely fine-hairy on midrib and nerves beneath, often the upper surface dark coloured to nearly black when dry and the undersurface olive brown, ± elliptic, with cuneate-attenuate base, crenate margin and mostly abruptly acuminate apex, 5.5–15 by 2.2–6 cm; acumen 5–15 mm; nerves 5–9 pairs, usually meeting in the intramarginal reticulation; reticulation rather fine or coarse; petiole 3–15 mm. Raceme often basally branched, axis fine-hairy to appressed-pubescent, 3–12 cm; bracts and bracteoles soon caducous, 2–3 and ca 1.5 mm long respectively; pedicels with same indumentum as on axis, 1–5 mm. Calyx glabrous, 1.5–2.5 mm; lobes ciliate, when young 1–1.5 mm, becoming longer by tearing apart. Corolla 4–6 mm. Stamens 40 to ca 60. Disk glabrous to sparsely hairy or pilose, especially after anthesis. Ovary glabrous, ca 1 mm high; style glabrous, 4–5 mm. Fruit orbicular, pink, green, yellow, or dark blue (sec. coll.) 4–10(–20) by 3–8(–15) mm; mesocarp thin, fleshy; stone smooth, cells 3, but usually only 1 fertile, the sterile cells larger than the fertile ones, filled with air towards the base. Seed and embryo U-shaped.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Symplocos celastrifolia. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 456. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Tree to 25 m; twigs often spreadingly thin-pilose on innovations; growth discontinuous; terminal buds with many leathery scales, pilose or glabrous, the latter leaving obvious scars. Leaves spreadingly to more or less appressed-long-pilose beneath, especially on midrib and nerves, sometimes entirely glabrous, with cuneate base, sharply dentate margin and acuminate apex, 7–16(–22) by 2–5(–7) cm; acumen 12–22 mm; nerves 6–13 pairs, meeting in a distinct looped intramarginal vein; reticulation fine, prominent; petiole slender, 15–25 mm. Spike resembling a short cone in bud, becoming at most 3 cm long; axis ± appressed-long-pilose to densely pubescent; bracts broadly ovoid to orbicular boat-shaped, appressed (silky-) pubescent on the back, at least in the middle, ca 5 by 5 mm; bracteoles with same indumentum, narrowly elliptic, ca 3 mm long, both soon caducous. Calyx glabrous or slightly pubescent, 2.5–4 mm, the lobes initially 1–1.5 mm, becoming often as long as the calyx by tearing apart. Corolla ca 5 mm. Stamens 30 to more than 100. Disk glabrous. Ovary glabrous, 1–1.5 mm high; style glabrous, but the conical base sometimes hairy. Fruit ellipsoid, 22–40 by 8–18 mm; mesocarp thick, corky; stone with 8 high ridges, 3-celled with a central canal, often only one cell developed. Seed cylindrical, with straight embryo.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Symplocos cerasifolia. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 454. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Small shrub to large tree. Leaves very variable in all characters. Inflorescence with spicate branches. Fruit globose to ampulliform with curved embryo and seed.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Symplocos cochinchinensis. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 455. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Shrub or small tree, rarely a large tree to 45 m high and 80 cm diam; twigsrusty tomentose or velvet, glabrescent, rarely pubescent appressed-pilose, or glabrous; terminal buds hairy. Leaves rusty or brownish pubescent or tomentose beneath, especially on midrib and nerves, rarely glabrous, (ovate) to elliptic to (obovate) with cuneate, rarely rounded base, glandular dentate or crenulate margin and more or less acuminate apex, (6–)12–25 by (2.5–)3–1 cm; nerves (8–)10–14(–16) pairs, very prominent beneath, parallel to each other, mostly quite straight, curved upwards towards the margin and nearly reaching it, whether forming an intramarginal vein or not; reticulation usually rather fine; petiole (2–)5–17 mm. Inflorescence with spicate branches, 3–15 cm, axis densely rusty tomentose or pubescent; bracts and bracteoles persistent, with same indumentum, the former at least 2 mm long and wide, but usually longer, exceptionally up to 10 mm long, with the 2 smaller bracteoles forming a calycle hiding the ovary. Flowers faintly scented to fragrant. Calyx (appressed-pubescent) divided into (1–)2(–3) mm long lobes. Corolla white (according to some collectors with a yellow spot on each lobe) 3–5 mm long. Stamens 30–70. Disk glabrous. Ovary glabrous, 0.5–1 mm high; style glabrous, 3–5 mm. Fruit ampulliform or globose, 5–7 by 4–5 mm, more or less ribbed when dry, often narrowed into a cylindrical neck, crowned by the usually closed, enlarged calyx lobes which form a conical beak on top; mesocarp thin, fleshy. Seed 1, twice curved with similar curved embryo.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Symplocos cochinchinensis cochinchinensis. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 455. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Twigs and leaves glabrous, except sometimes the very youngest parts;terminal buds hairy or glabrous. Leaves elliptic with cuneate base and acuminate apex, 4.5–21 by (1.5–)2.5–8 cm; nerves 6–9 pairs (but in forms transitional to var. cochinchinensis up to 13 pairs), not strictly parallel, anastomosing at some distance of the margin, often meeting in an intramarginal vein; reticulation often quite coarse; petiole (5–)10–15(–20) mm (in transitional forms the leaves are like those of var. cochinchinensis except for the indumentum). Spike 1.5–14 cm, axis glabrous to more or less apressed-puberulous or pubescent; bracts and bracteoles persistent, at most 2 mm long and broad, but usually only 1 mm, only enveloping the base of the ovary; a short pedicel exceptionally present. Calyx glabrous or nearly so, divided into 1–2 mm long, often ciliate lobes, not elongating in fruit, whether closed after anthesis or not; other characters as in var. cochinchinensis. Fruit as in var. cochinchinensis.
creator: Rachun Pooma
bibliographicCitation: Symplocos cochinchinensis laurina. Flora of Thailand. Vol. 2. Part 4, 1981. Pg. 456. Accessed 2021-07-31

description: Shrub or small tree to 18 m; twigs glabrous or pubescent to appressed orspreadingly-long-hairy, sometimes with a mixed indumentum of a short tomentum and long spreading hairs; terminal buds hairy. Leaves (narrowly) elliptic to ovate, sparsely appressed-pilose or nearly glabrous to densely-appressed to spreadingly- long-hairy beneath, rarely also hairy above, with cordate to cuneate base, recurved, entire to glandular denticulate margin and acuminate apex, 6–27 by 1.1–8.5 cm; acumen 5–30 mm; nerves 3–11 pairs; reticulation fine (handlens!); petiole 1–10 mm. Spikes short, often clustered, to 1(–2) cm, from the axils of the upper leaves, rarely flowers solitary, axis subglabrous to appressed-pubescent, or with long, spreading to appressed, stiff, brown to rusty hairs 1–4 mm long; bracts and bracteoles persistent, (broadly) ovate, triangular or semi-elliptic, rarely acuminate, hairy. Calyx hairy or glabrous, whether entirely divided into lobes or not. Corolla 2.5–6 mm. Stamens ca 30 to ca 100. Disk glabrous. Ovary hairy, 1–2 mm high; style glabrous, but often with conical, hairy base. Fruit mostly 1–2 from each inflorescence, glabrous or sparsely long-hairy, bright blue in vivo, cylindrical, narrowed towards the apex, 13–18 by 3–5 mm; mesocarp crustaceous; stone with ca 12 longitudinal grooves; cells 1–3. Seeds usually 1, straight with straight embryo.

description: Twigs glabrous or rarely appressed-pubescent. Leaves usually sparsely appressed-pilose below, nearly glabrous, the hairs very inconspicuous, 8.5–18 by 3–8.5 cm, long-acuminate with entire to sharply dentate margin; nerves 4–9 pairs; petiole 3–7 mm. Inflorescence a contracted often branched spike 1(–2) cm long; axis from nearly glabrous to appressed-pubescent; bract and bracteoles ovate to triangular, appressed-pubescent, 1–1.5 and ca 1 mm long respectively. description: Shrub or small tree to 12 m; twigs glabrous, except the base of the young shoot which is pubescent between the scars of the fallen bud scales; terminal buds often large, with coriaceous glabrous outer scales, and hairy inner scales. Leaves (narrowly) obovate to elliptic, 9–23 by 3–6 cm, glabrous with cuneate base and acuminate apex; acumen 5–18 mm; nerves 9–18 pairs; reticulation coarse; petiole often stout, 10–20 mm. Inflorescence forming a cone in bud, the base surrounded by several glabrous, coriaceous scales; raceme to 10(–15) cm; axis sparsely soft hairy to densely (appressed) sericeous; bracts appressed-pubescent to sericeous, 5–9 mm; bracteoles pubescent, ca 3 mm, both soon caducous; pedicels becoming 2–10 mm. Calyx glabrous or rarely sericeous towards the apex, triangular (to semi-elliptic), 1–1.5 mm long. Corolla 5–6(–10) mm. Stamens 40–75. Disk inconspicuous. Ovary glabrous, 1–2 mm high; style glabrous, but the conical base minutely soft-hairy to densely sericeous. Fruit ellipsoid, 5–12 by 3–7 mm with smooth stone; mesocarp fleshy. Seed 1, from nearly straight to curved.

description: Shrub, or less often a tree to 22 m high and 50 cm diam; twigs sparsely pilose, puberulous, or appressed-pubescent, glabrescent, often zig-zag; terminal buds hairy. Leaves alternately or (on the leaders) spirally arranged, glabrous above, sparsely finely adpressed-hairy beneath, rarely patently hirsute, especially on midrib and nerves and towards the margin, (narrowly) elliptic or sometimes ovate, acuminate to caudate with acute to rounded base, 5–13(–18) by 2–4.5(–6) cm; acumen 5–20 mm; margin entire or glandular, but glands hot closely spaced; nerves (4–)6–8(–11) pairs, meeting in a looped intramarginal vein; reticulation coarse; petiole 2–8 mm. Flowers in a fascicle of reduced, often branched, racemes to 2.5 cm long; bracts and bracteoles persistent, minute (rarely to 3 mm), like the axis pubescent; often several bracts present, indicating origin from a more branched inflorescence; pedicels 1–5 mm, pubescent. Calyx divided into (4–)5(–6) broadly ovoid, rounded, appressed-pubescent or glabrous lobes, ca 1 mm long but sometimes the lobes different in size, often some of the lobes petaloid. Corolla glabrous or more often with minute hairs towards the outer base, rarely some hairs on the back also, 2–4.5 mm. Stamens 12–35. Disk glabrous to more or less pilose, low annular. Ovary appressed-hairy, ca 1 mm high; style hairy, especially towards the thickened base, rarely glabrous, 2–3.5 mm. Fruit broadly or narrowly ampulliform, often curved, the belly globose or ovoid, the neck broadly conical, 5–7 by 3–5 mm; mesocarp thin, rather fleshy, or papyraceous; stone ruminate with ca 10 shallow grooves or not ruminate. Seed 1 much lobed with slightly curved embryo.

description: Shrub or tree to 30 m; terminal buds hairy. Leaves elliptic, 7–17 by 3–7.5 cm, glabrous above, glabrous beneath or the midrib sparsely short fine hairy; base cuneate; acumen 3–20 mm; nerves 5–11 pairs; reticulation rather fine to coarse; petiole 5–15 mm. Flowers in a raceme to 10 cm, including bract and bracteoles light grey to rusty tomentose; pedicels 0–6 mm, with 2 or 3 tiny bracteoles. Calyx (including the ovary) ca 6(–10) mm long. Corolla 25–50 mm, the upper ¼ to ½ free; tube 3–4 mm wide, lobes spreading or recurved. Staminal tube ca 5 mm shorter than corolla, adnate to its tube except towards the apex; anthers 20–110. Ovary semi-inferior, 3–4 celled, crowned by the style which is slightly longer than the stamens; stigma knob-shaped Fruit dull green in vivo, narrowly obovoid to spindle-shaped, often oblique or curved, 30–50 by 20–30 mm; mesocarp fleshy; stone smooth.

description: Shrub or tree to 15 m; twigs glabrous; terminal buds glabrous. Leaves obovate, 14–22 cm by 4–12 cm, glabrous with cuneate base and acuminate apex; acumen 3–15 mm; nerves 6–11 pairs, meeting in an intramarginal vein; reticulation usually fine; petiole 12–30 mm. Inflorescence forming a cone in bud, conspicuous by the light grey appressed-pubescent bracts, or cone dark brown and bracts glabrous, becoming at most 5 cm long; bracts 5–8 mm, falling as soon as the flower matures; bracteoles 1–3 mm, falling during anthesis; pedicels 1–3 mm. Calyx glabrous, often wholly divided into 1–3 mm long lobes. Corolla 6–9 mm. Stamens ca 80. Disk flat or cylindrical, shortly pubescent. Ovary glabrous, 1–2 mm high; style glabrous, 5–8 mm. Fruit elliptic to cylindrical, often slightly narrowed to the apex, 13–24 by 5–9 mm; mesocarp rather hard. Seed 1, straight.

description: Shrub or tree to 10 m; twigs glabrous; terminal buds pubescent. Leaves glabrous obovate to elliptic, 11–24 by 4–6 cm with cuneate base and acuminate apex; nerves 6–11 pairs, meeting in a distinct intramarginal vein; acumen 7–20 mm; reticulation rather fine (handlens); petiole 5–12 mm. Inflorescence forming a short cone in bud, growing out to 4(–7) cm; axis glabrous; bracts and bracteoles caducous, appressed-pubescent; pedicels 0–1 mm. Fruit ca ovoid, gradually narrowed towards the apex, 15–28 by 4–10 mm; mesocarp fleshy, thin; stone with low but distinct ridges. Seed 1, straight.

description: Shrub or tree to 15 m; twigs glabrous, yellowish green, angular when dry; terminal buds glabrous. Leaves coriaceous (sometimes quite thin), glabrous, acute or obtuse with cuneate base and entire or glandular dentate revolute margin, ca elliptic, 5–12 by 2–4.5 cm; acumen 5–25 mm; midrib more or less prominent on the upper surface, often sulcate towards the base; nerves 5–15 pairs, prominent on both upper and lower surface; reticulation often obscure; petiole 5–15 mm. Flowers in a basally branched short dense raceme or condensed spike of 1.5–4 cm; axis puberulous or pubescent; bracts and bracteoles persistent under the fruit, glabrous, or sometimes pubescent or puberulous on midrib and base, 1–3 mm; pedicels 0–5 mm. Calyx mostly glabrous, nearly divided into 5 lobes, 1–3 mm. Corolla 3–5 mm. Stamens 10–70. Disk densely hairy. Ovary glabrous, 0.5–2 mm high; style glabrous, or hairy, mostly towards the base. Fruit ellipsoid (to rarely nearly orbicular), 1–3-celled, 5–18 by 4–15 mm, the wider ones with 2 seeds; mesocarp fleshy. Seeds usually U-shaped with U-shaped embryo, in the 3-celled fruits the seeds abortive or (at most) V-shaped; the legs of the U are either separated by a septum or not.

description: Tree ca 15 m; twigs glabrous; terminal buds glabrous or appressed-pubescent. Leaves glabrous, obovate, 12–19 by 4.5–8 cm; base cuneate; apex acuminate; acumen 2–6 mm; margin glandular, dentate to crenate; nerves 9–13 pairs, meeting in an intramarginal vein at least towards the apex of the leaf; reticulation fine, prominent; petiole 15–20 mm. Inflorescence a spike; axis glabrous, becoming at most 4 cm in fruit; bracts caducous, appressed-pubescent but the outer ones glabrous, 5–10 mm; bracteoles glabrous, to 5 mm. Calyx 3–5 mm, the lobes pubescent both inside and outside, 1–2 mm long, tearing apart when older and thus the limb becoming symmetrical or ca 3-lobed. Corolla ca 4 mm. Stamens ca 70. Disk glabrous, 5-glandular. Ovary glabrous, 1.5–2 mm high; style glabrous with broadly conical base. Fruit ellipsoid to cylindrical, 30–35 by ca 15 mm; mesocarp hard, corky; stone woody, very hard with many shallow longitudinal ridges, 3-celled with a central canal. Seeds straight with straight embryo.

description: Twigs glabrous. Inflorescence a basally branched raceme to 4 cm; axis puberulous; bracts and bracteoles caducous or the bracteoles persistent, puberulous, 0.5–1 mm: pedicels puberulous, to 1.5, or sometimes to 3 mm in the lowermost flower. description: Shrub with densely patently long-pilose twigs, hairs longer than 2 mm ;terminal buds small, pubescent. Leaves ovate, glabrous, 7–11 by 3–5 cm, base cordate, apex acuminate, margin denticulate; nerves 7–8 pairs, meeting in an intramarginal vein; reticulation very fine but hardly prominent; petiole ca 4 mm. Inflorescence a long peduncled raceme to 3 cm; peduncle 1–3 cm long, with the axis patently pubescent; bracts and bracteoles persistent, appressed-pubescent, 2–3 and 2 mm long respectively; pedicels 1–4 mm. Calyx glabrous, 1.5 mm long, the lobes ca 1.25 mm. Corolla ca 4 mm. Stamens 50–100. Disk 5-glandular, with the conical style base sparsely pilose. Ovary densely pubescent, ca 0.5 mm high. description: Shrub or treelet to 5 m (rarely decidious sec. coll.); terminal budshairy; twigs glabrous or rarely hairy, often soon thickened and then with a spongy grey bark. Leaves ± elliptic, 8–15 by 1.5–5(–8) cm, glabrous (or young leaves appressed-long-hairy), often the upper cuticle very thick and wrinkled when dry; base attenuate, cuneate to rounded, apex rounded to acuminate, blunt; nerves 5–9 pairs, merged into the venation or an intramarginal vein present; reticulation coarse; petiole 7–15 mm. Inflorescence an axillary, sometimes branched, raceme (lowermost flowers always pedicelled) to 10(–17) cm; axis pubescent to woolly or tomentose; bracts 3–4 mm, bracteoles 2–3 mm, both appressed-pubescent and caducous; pedicels (0.5–)1–3(–8) mm. Calyx glabrous, 1.5–3 mm, the lobes 0.25–0.5 mm shorter, rarely minutely appressed-hairy to pubescent. Corolla 5–6 mm. Stamens ca 100. Disk low cylindrical, 5-glandular, shortly to woolly hairy. Ovary glabrous, 1–1.5(–2) mm high; style glabrous, or hairy towards the base. Fruit ellipsoid, 8–11 by 4–10 mm, 2–3-celled; mesocarp fleshy; stone smooth. Seed mostly 1, straight.

description: Low shrub to medium sized tree; twigs glabrous (or nearly so), on innovationssometimes hairy; terminal buds usually hairy. Leaves glabrous, 2–10 by 0.75–4.5 cm; margin glandular dentate, denticulate or crenulate; base attenuate; apex acuminate to caudate, acumen 3–20 mm; nerves 5–8 pairs, meeting in a rather inconspicuous intramarginal vein close to the margin; reticulation fine to rather coarse; petiole 2–10 mm. Inflorescence a few to many-flowered axillary raceme, 1–6 mm long, the base surrounded by several cataphylls; axis and the 0.5–13 mm long pedicels from nearly glabrous to pilose or pubescent; bract at base of pedicel, appressed-hairy, 2–5 mm; bracteoles under the flower 0.5–4 mm, both very soon caducous. Calyx glabrous to (sparsely) appressed-hairy, divided into the ciliate 0.35–1.5 mm long lobes which are much shorter to slightly longer than the ovary. Corolla 4–8(–11) mm. Stamens 25–40. Disk glabrous, mostly annular. Ovary glabrous to shortly appressed-hairy, 1–2 mm high; style glabrous. Fruit ovoid to ampulliform, 6–10 by 3–6 mm; mesocarp chartaceous, brittle when dry; stone shallowly ruminate. Seed curved, embryo once or twice curved.
